text.content:
The white route goes east to Kalaman, then trusts ships to carry the party around the Northern Wastes to Mirivale, Hylo, Gilthanost, and finally the approaches to Wayreth.

LegNormal timeExpected window if departing 20 Darkember
Vogler → Kalaman1 day mounted/boat; 1–2 on foot20–22 Darkember
Kalaman → Mirivale10–13 days sailing4–8 Frostkolt
Mirivale → Hylo4–6 days sailing8–15 Frostkolt
Hylo → Gilthanost5–7 days sailing17–22 Frostkolt
Gilthanost → Wayreth3–5 days21–24 Frostkolt

Reading These Windows

Every window above is an arrival window for a normal journey, and each already includes the short stops described on that leg's page. They are not best-case figures. The whole-route totals below are the ones to quote at the table.

How the journey goesDays from VoglerReaches WayrethAgainst the 26 Frostkolt deadline
Excellent — fast ships, no weather~2618 FrostkoltEight days spare
Normal29–3221–24 FrostkoltTwo to five days spare
Bad winter seas34–3626–28 FrostkoltOn the deadline or past it

Route Identity

The party gives up control over roads in exchange for continuous movement. The central questions become: Can they secure a ship? Can they keep it moving? What do they do when helping someone costs weather they may never get back?

The longest line on the map and, with a good captain, one of the quickest beneath your feet. Ships have the happy habit of continuing to travel while you sleep.

— Ispin Greenshield

The first leg is short enough to feel almost comfortable, which makes Kalaman’s scale and military anxiety hit harder.

TravelUse
1 day mounted or by boatTransition from village tragedy to the wider world
1–2 days on footUse only if the party lacks transport or deliberately travels slowly

Road Scenes

  1. Vogler’s Wake. Refugees and travelers carry different versions of what happened. The party hears their own recent actions turned into rumor.
  2. The Empty Riverboat. A small commercial boat drifts loose with no crew aboard. Investigation reveals frightened civilians abandoned it after seeing unfamiliar armed scouts.
  3. First Moon Check. A navigator or mage confirms that the party’s date calculation is correct: the conjunction cannot be negotiated with.

Information

  • Kalaman can provision a long voyage properly.
  • Captains are already charging more for uncertain northern routes.
  • Military authorities are beginning to ask who is traveling and why.

Kalaman is where Route I succeeds or fails. The party needs a vessel, a captain, and terms that will survive worsening news.

Expected dateSuggested playPrimary decision
20–22 DarkemberHalf to one full sessionTake the first reliable berth, bargain for a better ship, or spend precious time waiting

Arrival

Make the port loud, crowded, and useful: shipwrights, warehouses, military patrols, caravans, sailors, factors, and people offering passage to anyone who can pay. The party should feel that nearly anything can be purchased here except certainty.

Campaign NPCs

  • Captain Mara Vey: blunt, experienced, and unwilling to promise an arrival date she cannot defend.
  • Factor Dalen Orr: knows which captains are solvent, which are smugglers, and which ships are about to be requisitioned.
  • Navren Pell: a moon-watching navigator who recognizes Ispin’s markings and can verify the route around the Northern Wastes.

Scenes

  1. The Three Offers. Cheap/slow, expensive/reliable, or fast/questionable. Each ship should create a different complication later.
  2. Requisition Order. A military official claims one civilian vessel hours before departure. The party can negotiate, invoke favors, or scramble for another berth.
  3. Missing Cargo. A crate meant for Mirivale has been stolen. Recovering it earns reduced passage and a captain who now owes the party.

Knowledge Available

  • Mirivale is the next proper port worth planning around.
  • The northern sweep is long but avoids mountain and border crossings.
  • Winter weather is the route’s true enemy.

GM Note — Departure Clock

Allow one day to find passage without penalty. Every additional full day spent shopping for a “perfect” ship should move the calendar.

pages.name: Leg 2: Kalaman to Mirivale — Around the Northern Wastes

text.content:
Ten to thirteen days at sea creates room for relationships, weather, pursuit, and the realization that the party cannot simply step off the route when something goes wrong.

Sea Rhythm

Do not play ten identical days. Use three or four strong beats: departure, first hard weather, one encounter or discovery, and the final approach to Mirivale.

Travel Challenge

Successes before failuresOutcome
5 successes before 3 failuresArrive within the normal 10–13 day window.
3 failures firstAdd 1 day and one ship complication.
Major failure during a stormAdd 2 days or force an emergency stop/repair.

Useful Skills

Survival for weather, Perception for hazards, Athletics for rigging, Vehicles (water) for seamanship, Arcana for magical weather, Medicine for shipboard injury, Persuasion or Intimidation for crew morale.

If somebody tells you their ship can make Mirivale in six days, ask what kind of dragon is pulling it.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Shipboard Life: Make the Voyage a Place

text.content:
A sea route should not become a travel montage with occasional initiative. The ship is a temporary settlement with hierarchy, routines, grudges, and nowhere to walk away.

Recurring Shipboard Scenes

  • Watch at midnight: private conversations beneath all three moons.
  • Galley politics: sailors trading rumors from Palanthas, Solamnia, Ergoth, and the east.
  • Rope and canvas: a practical task lets martial characters matter during magical or weather-heavy travel.
  • Passenger secrets: merchants, refugees, robe-wearing mages, spies, or Krell can all become impossible to ignore aboard a confined vessel.

Shipboard Reputation

Track the crew as Hostile, Wary, Neutral, Friendly, or Loyal. Good conduct, useful work, fair division of danger, and saving a sailor shift the rating upward. Theft, arrogance, endangering the ship, or hiding a serious threat shifts it down.

pages.name: Stop 2: Mirivale — Beds, Repairs, and News

text.content:
Mirivale is the first proper reset after the northern sweep: a port where the party can repair equipment, change ships, and discover how much the world changed while they were at sea.

Expected arrivalSuggested playPrimary function
4–8 FrostkoltHalf session to one sessionResupply, news, ship decision, route confirmation

Arrival

Give the party a sharp contrast to shipboard confinement: crowded docks, dry ground, hot food, inns, and people who know the Straits of Algoni. If the voyage was rough, even a stable floor feels luxurious.

Campaign NPCs

  • Dockmaster Sera Tan: can find a vessel bound toward Hylo but refuses to move ships during obviously unsafe weather.
  • Old Varn: a retired sailor who sailed with Ispin once and has an embarrassing story the party has never heard.
  • Ellin Mareth: a courier with contradictory maps of Wayreth collected from different wizards.

Scenes

  1. Storm Damage. The party’s ship needs repairs. Pay, help, switch ships, or accept a one-day delay.
  2. The Wrong Map. Three maps place Wayreth in three different locations. None is obviously forged.
  3. War News. A new ship arrives carrying wounded soldiers or displaced families, raising War Pressure without requiring combat.

Knowledge Available

  • Hylo is sheltered and culturally unlike the war-touched ports behind them.
  • Gilthanost will require more careful diplomacy than Mirivale.
  • Wayreth’s contradictory maps are not merely cartographic incompetence.

pages.name: Leg 3: Mirivale to Hylo — The Straits of Algoni

text.content:
This four-to-six-day leg narrows the route and changes the campaign’s mood from cold open water to a busier, stranger maritime corridor.

Travel Beats

  1. Traffic. Kender craft, merchant ships, fishing boats, and vessels carrying stories from Ergoth make the sea feel inhabited.
  2. False Distress. A small vessel signals for aid. It may be genuinely damaged, a smuggler afraid of inspection, or a baited trap depending on the campaign’s pressure.
  3. The Moons Over the Strait. A clear night gives any arcane character a visceral sense that the three moons are moving toward a rare shared pattern.

Time

Normal arrival costs no extra days. Rescuing a nearby vessel can be resolved inside the travel leg; escorting it far off course costs one.

Hylo is a deliberate tonal release before the southern voyage becomes politically difficult again.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
8–15 FrostkoltHalf to one full sessionHumor, cultural contrast, rumor exchange, optional adventure

Arrival

Let the party experience a place where curiosity is normal and ownership is interpreted more flexibly than most travelers find comfortable. The war should feel distant here, not nonexistent.

Campaign NPCs

  • Pipkin “Three-Pockets” Vale: insists he knew Ispin and can prove it with an object Ispin definitely used to own.
  • Harborwarden Tessa Quickstep: cheerful, competent, and completely unimpressed by outsiders panicking about misplaced belongings.
  • Rollo Mapwhistle: has six route sketches to Gilthanost, four of which he drew from memory.

Scenes

  1. Inventory Day. Something important is missing and three unrelated things have appeared in the party’s packs. Recovering the original item is social, not punitive.
  2. The Story Contest. Ispin’s adventures are known here in wildly transformed versions. Players can correct the record or make it worse.
  3. A Boat Nobody Owns. A perfectly usable small craft has “temporarily lost track of its captain,” creating a moral and logistical temptation.

Knowledge Available

  • Southern waters carry more elven traffic.
  • Gilthanost is a sensible point to request Qualinesti help.
  • Someone matching a pursuer’s description may already have asked about the party.

Count your belongings before leaving. Then count the new belongings you do not remember owning.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 4: Hylo to Gilthanost — South to Qualinesti

text.content:
The final long sailing leg should steadily replace the openness of the sea with signs that the party is approaching territory where permission matters.

Visual Progression

  • More elven vessels and disciplined pilots.
  • Older coastal ruins and abandoned settlements.
  • Fewer captains willing to discuss exact landing places casually.
  • Lookouts challenge ships before the party sees any formal harbor authority.

Complication Choices

  1. Elven Inspection. Declare weapons, purpose, magical affiliations, and the reason for seeking Wayreth.
  2. Shadowed Sail. A vessel follows at extreme distance for half a day. It may be a pursuer, patrol, or nervous merchant.
  3. Bad Wind. Lose speed or risk sail damage by pressing on.

Gilthanost is the point where the Sailor’s Road stops being about ships and becomes a problem of elven trust, guides, and the nature of Wayreth.

Expected arrivalSuggested playPrimary function
17–22 FrostkoltOne sessionQualinesti diplomacy, final resupply, Wayreth lore

Arrival

The party has traveled a continent to reach a place where simply announcing “we seek the Tower of High Sorcery” is not enough. Their invitation matters, their conduct matters, and any robe-affiliated character may be judged through a political lens.

Campaign NPCs

  • Laereth Silverbough: border official who values precision and dislikes Ispin’s habit of turning serious matters into stories.
  • Miravel Thalas: guide familiar with the outer approaches to the Forest but unable to promise where it will appear.
  • Seren Dawnleaf: elven mage who can identify the invitation’s connection to Wayreth and becomes cautious at the Master’s seal.

Scenes

  1. The Petition. Explain who summoned them, why they seek Wayreth, and why armed outsiders should be assisted.
  2. The Missing Guide. A guide expected from the interior has vanished; finding them reveals someone else is also trying to reach the Forest.
  3. The Six Maps. Elven records deliberately preserve multiple contradictory locations for Wayreth.

Knowledge Available

  • The Forest is an active threshold, not an ordinary woodland.
  • Candidates can arrive at the correct region and still fail to reach the Tower.
  • The three Orders coexist institutionally even when their motives differ sharply.

pages.name: Final Leg: Gilthanost to the Forest of Wayreth

text.content:
The last three-to-five days should feel increasingly unlike geographic travel.

Day One

Roads and trails still function. Guides can name hills, streams, and distances.

Day Two

A familiar landmark appears too early or on the wrong side of the trail. Maps disagree with the ground.

Day Three

The party finds signs of passage that could only be their own, despite never walking the route before.

Day Four+

Navigation checks stop answering “where is Wayreth?” and instead answer “what does the Forest appear to be asking of you?”

GM Note — End at the Border

The road arc ends when the party has unquestionably reached the influence of the Forest. The existing Wayreth material then takes over.

These encounters are written to reveal setting, route, or character information rather than merely consume resources.

d12Encounter
1A military courier ship refuses to stop but signals a warning about weather behind it.
2A kender passenger insists a party keepsake belongs in a museum and can explain exactly how it came into their possession.
3A drifting lifeboat contains three survivors and a sealed Dragonarmy dispatch case.
4A pod of strange sea creatures follows the vessel for hours; sailors treat their behavior as a weather omen.
5A Red Robe passenger asks an arcane PC what they believe the Test is actually for.
6A sudden squall tears rigging; the encounter is a skill challenge, not combat.
7A merchant vessel reports a port the party expected to use is refusing arrivals for one day.
8A night lookout sees a second set of ship lights matching every turn.
9A sailor recognizes Ispin’s name and tells a story none of the party created.
10An elven patrol boards peacefully but asks very specific questions about Wayreth.
11A crate breaks open during rough weather, revealing contraband magical components.
12The sea goes unnaturally still beneath three visible moons; every arcane character feels watched.

pages.name: Route I: d12 Rumors and Knowledge

text.content:
Use these at docks, aboard ship, or over meals. Some are true, some incomplete, and some deliberately wrong.

d12Rumor
1“Kalaman captains are being paid twice: once to carry cargo, once to report passengers.”
2“Mirivale has three different maps of Wayreth locked in the same archive.”
3“A Black Robe crossed the northern sea ahead of you.”
4“The moons have not aligned like this in living memory.”
5“Hylo has never lost anything. People simply forget where ownership moved.”
6“Elven pilots can find Wayreth whenever they wish.”
7“No. Elven pilots can find the forest. That is not the same thing.”
8“Dragonarmy agents have started buying charts of southern ports.”
9“A ship that carries a wizard under Nuitari should never sail without a second compass.”
10“The Test kills people because the Orders want fewer wizards.”
11“Ispin once crossed this water in a fishing boat with one oar.”
12“If you arrive at Wayreth on the Night itself, the Tower chooses the order of events for you.”

pages.name: Route I: Weather and Navigation Complications

text.content:
Weather is the route’s primary schedule threat. Make forecasts useful so players can make informed risks.

ConditionChoiceConsequence
HeadwindWait for better wind or continue slowlyWait: +1 day but safe. Continue: no full delay on a successful challenge; +1 day on failure.
Squall lineReef sail early or try to outrun itReefing costs speed; outrunning risks damage.
FogReduce speed or navigate aggressivelyAggressive navigation can produce a wrong-coast complication.
Damaged mastRepair in port or jury-rig at seaPort repair costs time/coin; jury-rig creates disadvantage on next weather challenge.
Captain injuredPCs assist command or divertSuccessful assistance keeps schedule.
Port closureWait or seek a lesser landingWaiting costs 1 day; lesser landing creates a local adventure.

pages.name: Route I: Krell, Skaith, and Mereth at Sea

text.content:
The confined nature of a ship turns pursuit into suspicion and social pressure.

Krell

Place him aboard the Kalaman vessel or have him transfer at Mirivale. He is using forged or stolen crew papers and initially claims he is simply fleeing the war.

Discovery

  1. A sailor finds blood on a bunk after Krell rebinds hidden markings.
  2. The ship’s papers list a crewman who died two ports ago.
  3. Krell reacts too strongly to the Master’s seal or to a discussion of Wayreth.

Skaith

Skaith can appear as Krell on another deck, leave contradictory evidence, or impersonate a sailor who “saw” the party sheltering a fugitive.

Mereth

Mereth prefers landfall. She waits at Mirivale, Hylo, or Gilthanost and makes a direct argument: carrying Krell into Wayreth is more dangerous than killing him now.

pages.name: Route I Signature Adventure: The Black Lantern

text.content:
This one-session sea adventure can be inserted between Kalaman and Mirivale without changing the route.

Hook

A black lantern burns aboard a merchant ship found drifting across the party’s course. Its sails are intact, its cargo is aboard, and nobody answers.

Truth

The crew abandoned ship after a magical object in the hold began projecting memories and voices into their sleep. Dragonarmy couriers were moving the object west for study.

Scenes

  1. Board the drifting ship during worsening weather.
  2. Search cabins where each PC hears a different familiar voice.
  3. Find the locked courier hold and surviving officer.
  4. Decide whether to destroy, keep, surrender, or conceal the object before the storm arrives.

Reward

Documents provide military intelligence and evidence that enemy agents are interested in magical routes and lunar events.

Time

Resolved decisively: no extra day. Towing the ship to port: +1 day.

pages.name: Route I Signature Adventure: The Borrowed Map of Hylo

text.content:
This lighter Hylo adventure turns kender curiosity into a real route problem without making theft the only joke.

Hook

Ispin’s marked map disappears during a public storytelling contest. Three different kender honestly believe they are returning it.

Complication

One “copy” is actually an older High Sorcery map with different Wayreth markings. Another contains notes from someone who recently asked about the same Gilthanost approach.

Scenes

  1. Trace the map through a chain of enthusiastic borrowers.
  2. Win or survive a storytelling contest about Ispin.
  3. Compare the three maps and identify the dangerous new annotation.
  4. Choose whether to report the suspicious traveler to Hylo authorities.

Reward

The party gains a second Wayreth map and a clue concerning a pursuer or Krell’s route.

Time

No delay if completed before the ship’s scheduled departure; +1 day if the party misses the tide.

pages.name: Route I: Optional Adventures and Expansion

text.content:
Use these to extend the route toward 14–16 sessions without altering its geography.

LocationAdventureCore choice
KalamanThe Requisitioned ShipHelp the military and lose a berth, or prove civilians still have a claim on the vessel.
Northern SeaThe Black LanternTake military intelligence from a drifting cursed courier ship.
MirivaleThe Three MapsDetermine why three respected maps disagree about Wayreth.
HyloThe Borrowed MapRecover Ispin’s map and discover a more important one.
GilthanostThe Missing GuideFind the elf who was supposed to lead the party toward the Forest.
Final approachThe Road Behind YouThe party encounters evidence that somebody has been following the same impossible path.

Keep at least one sea complication social or investigative. Route I loses its identity if every problem is solved by fighting pirates.

pages.name: Route I Finale: From Coastline to Impossible Forest

text.content:
Route I should end with the party realizing that surviving the sea did not buy them certainty—only the opportunity to be judged by Wayreth itself.

Expected Arrival

ConditionsWayreth window
Excellent — ~26 daysAbout 18–20 Frostkolt
Normal — 29–32 daysAbout 21–24 Frostkolt
Storm-delayed — 34–36 days26–28 Frostkolt

Final Image

Behind them lies a route measured in harbors and nautical miles. Ahead, the marked road on Ispin’s map stops corresponding to any visible path. A tree bears a cut made yesterday by one of the characters—despite none of them having been here before.

When an elf tells you a forest path is nearby, ask whether they mean nearby to a human, an elf, or a tree.

— Ispin Greenshield
